subject: Renewal kickoff: Cumulus Health — term refresh + capacity uptick
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@cumulushealth.com>, Kyle Morris <kyle.morris@cumulushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal kickoff: Cumulus Health — term refresh + capacity uptick

Hi Elena / Kyle —

Thanks again for the upfront conversation last week. I wanted to kick off the formal renewal + capacity uptick thread so we can align timeline, stakeholders, and the QBR slot. High-level goals from our side:

- Lock a new 12‑month term with a staged commit that supports the 25% throughput uplift you indicated.
- Confirm governance and procurement stakeholders for SOC/contract review.
- Schedule a QBR/demo to walk technical implications and the runbook for burst capacity.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Can you confirm who will own procurement and security reviews on your side (names + emails)?
2) QBR window: Dec 9–11 — we have morning PT availability on Dec 10 or Dec 11. Please flag preferred date/time.
3) Internal ops ask: Ben/ David — please see the attached mutual action plan draft and a high-level capacity placeholder so we can estimate staging.

Attachments: Cumulus_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.xlsx (xlsx) — mutual action plan + initial milestone dates.

If helpful, I can send a short pre-QBR readout (15m) to sync technical owners before the main meeting.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Elena / team —

Quick technical ops notes while we wait for security contact:
- Preliminary throughput estimate: ~+25% token throughput based on your Q4 growth trend. That maps to ~1.25x peak GPU hours and a 20–25% increase in embedding units.
- Recommended approach: staged commit (baseline + scheduled bursts) + a dedicated burst pool for predictable performance during peak hours.
- Runbook: we'll prepare a short operational runbook covering autoscale triggers, cache warming, and KV cache migration steps.

I've attached a short capacity sketch (pdf) with the baseline vs uplift numbers — David, can you validate whether the %s are achievable on our current Dedicated pools or if we should propose a short-term burst allocation?

Attachments: capacity-estimate-cumulus.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal kickoff: Cumulus Health — term refresh + capacity uptick

Thanks everyone — quick capacity confirmation and next steps from infra: 

- Validation: The +25% uplift is within our Dedicated pool headroom but will need a temporary burst reservation during the first 6 weeks of ramp to ensure warm caches and steady latency. We can support the uplift with a short-lived burst allocation and then rebaseline to the committed capacity.
- Timeline proposal:
  * Dec 10 — QBR + contract/redline review (target 10:00 PT as requested). Please include procurement and security leads.
  * Dec 11–15 — legal & procurement review window; aim to finalize redlines by Dec 15.
  * Jan 4 — target go‑live for staged commit / baseline increase (after DocuSign and provisioning).
- Actions assigned:
  1) Olga — confirm QBR invite (I will attend for infra ops).
  2) Ben — finalize the 2‑page runbook and the capacity estimate (attach to QBR materials).
  3) Elena/Kyle — confirm security contact and procurement signoff owner on the DocuSign routing.
  4) Me (David) — provision burst pool once contracts are signed; will share provisioning ETA in the runbook.

I've uploaded a readout stub we can iterate on (runbook_stub.md). I'll also create a short provisioning checklist and share prior to QBR.

Calendar: QBR scheduled for Dec 10, 2026 at 10:00 PT — calendar invite sent separately.

Thanks,
David Kim
Director, Infrastructure Reliability, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai
